integrity.claim_scope: Compactly supported invariant probability measures in the strict positive octant for the printed linear-response shared-predation model; the sharper prey sorting rule additionally assumes equal fear sensitivity.
integrity.numerical_role: No numerical experiment is used in the proof; the accompanying computation checks exact symbolic identities only.
integrity.proof_basis: Invariant-measure Lie-derivative identities, an exact reciprocal Jensen-defect decomposition, uniqueness of the positive equilibrium, and scalar logistic rigidity.

scientific_limitations: The result is a necessary law for compact interior recurrence; it does not establish existence of recurrent non-equilibrium dynamics.
It does not resolve the source paper's global-stability conjecture.
The prey ordering independent of the invariant measure is proved only when the two fear sensitivities are equal.
A conceptually close 1998 shared-predation cycling paper could be compared only at abstract level, leaving a stated residual originality risk.
title: Mean-selection laws for recurrent states in a shared-predation fear model
